scope.description: Hand-researched deepening pass for Japanese Pokemon Jungle, emphasizing the 48-card second Japanese booster, all-with-rarity-symbol boundary, no English-style holo/non-holo duplication, Eeveelution forest memory, and cross-language identification rails.

claims.text: The local catalog, TCGdex, Pokellector, and Bulbapedia model Japanese Pokemon Jungle as released on March 5, 1997.
The local catalog, TCGdex, Pokellector, and Bulbapedia support a 48-card Japanese Pokemon Jungle checklist.

Bulbapedia describes Jungle as the second main expansion of the Pokemon Trading Card Game and says the Japanese release was Pokemon Jungle, based on Generation I Pokemon and associated with the Kanto Safari Zone setting.
The local catalog preserves Pokemon Jungle as release_family_id jp_tcg_jungle_19970305, a 48-row Japanese booster release without English-style holo/non-holo duplicate numbering.
The local pre-English symbol-status matrix and release map mark Japanese Pokemon Jungle as all-with-rarity-symbols, making it a post-Base comparison source rather than a No Rarity source.

The English Jungle history dossier records the later English release as a 64-row expansion with holo/non-holo duplication and no-symbol error folklore; those are English assembly features, not automatic properties of the Japanese 48-row release.

The local Japanese Jungle artist clusters are: Kagemaru Himeno (18 local rows; examples: Bellsprout, Butterfree, Weepinbell), Mitsuhiro Arita (15 local rows; examples: Venonat, Exeggcute, Rapidash), Ken Sugimori (11 local rows; examples: Nidoran♀, Paras, Nidorina), Keiji Kinebuchi (4 local rows; examples: Oddish, Gloom, Vileplume).

Japanese Pokemon Jungle matters because it is the first sequel habitat after the launch grammar: a compact 48-card forest where Eevee's futures, Safari-zone creature memory, Pikachu's common-row gravity, Scyther's sharp silhouette, and Snorlax's beloved obstruction all arrive before English expansion logic adds mirrors and errors.

Preserve Japanese row identity before comparing to English Jungle, Base Set 2, Legendary Collection, or no-symbol folklore.
steps: Preserve release_family_id jp_tcg_jungle_19970305, Japanese product name ポケモンジャングル, and the printed row number 001-048.
Do not infer English Jungle set id base2, English 64-card numbering, English holo/non-holo mirror identity, or English no-symbol error status from a Japanese Jungle row.
For No Rarity or missing-symbol claims, treat Japanese Jungle as a with-rarity-symbol post-Base comparison source unless direct evidence and a different sourced branch say otherwise.
For Eeveelutions, Scyther, Snorlax, Pikachu, or Poke Ball, compare row number and language before carrying any market, edition, error, or reprint memory into transaction logic.
Use seller scans and verifier judgment for possession, authenticity, condition, edition, and price; this catalog makes the branch questions legible only.

narrative.human_title: The first forest before the mirrors
narrative.why_it_matters: Japanese Pokemon Jungle is the sequel before the sequel gets complicated. It has no English-style holo/non-holo mirror rows, no English no-symbol error folklore, and no need to inflate itself to 64 cards. It is a tighter object: 48 cards, a forest after the launch-room grammar, and a page where Eevee can split three ways while Snorlax blocks the path and Scyther cuts through the grass. For the catalog, this is the clean branch that teaches comparison: same forest memory, different assembly.
